content:
maya: kicking off the Greenfield POC perf run now. objective: validate 4k sustained embed qps + tails for mixed search workload. will post quick numbers as we go.
noah: 👍 what's the traffic mix? embeds only or combined with generation?
maya: 80% embeddings (seq=64), 20% short-gen (seq=128, max_gen=64). running on Dedicated 6x A100 equivalent, model: emb-lite-3b-qa-quant. batching: adaptive with max_batch_tokens=8192, batch_timeout_ms=10.
sales-amy: greenfield asked about whether we can guarantee 95th latency <120ms for embeds at their 4k qps target. also pinged about burst pricing and security questionnaire timeline.
eli: quick sanity: 4k qps of short embeds -> tokens/sec ~ (64 tokens * 4000)/s = 256k tokens/s, check GPU mem and NVLink.
eng-zoe: started loadgen. early numbers: sustained qps 3.9k, embed p50=22ms, p95=140ms, p99=320ms. tail higher when short-gen starts.
ops-bot: autoscaler: pool usage 95% at 1943210120; reserved capacity at commit, burst not enabled.
maya: logs snippet: 
```
[1943210121] r=E123 slot=gpu-2 q=9 batch_tks=6800 p95=142ms p99=312ms gpu_util=88% nvlink=78% cache_hit=0.96
[1943210122] r=G201 slot=gpu-5 q=1 batch_tks=120 p95=18ms p99=60ms gpu_util=30% nvlink=12% cache_hit=0.98
[1943210123] r=E200 slot=gpu-3 q=15 batch_tks=8200 p95=220ms p99=650ms gpu_util=99% nvlink=91% cache_hit=0.72
```
noah: p99 jumping when batch_tokens > max or when nvlink saturates. can you toggle max_batch_tokens to 4096 and run a short trial?
eng-zoe: will also try enabling multi-device embedding kernel (reduction) to reduce NVLink pressure.
maya: ran 10m with max_batch_tokens=4096: embed p95=118ms, p99=260ms, sustained qps 3.95k. nice improvement but still over 120ms p95 target at times.
sales-amy: greenfield wants exact wording for the security questionnaire: timeline for SOC2 evidence and whether embeddings are encrypted at rest. i added a comment in their doc but need a concise reply.
infra-luis: SOC2: we have SOC2 type II in progress + can provide interim controls. embeddings at rest: yes encrypted via KMS; we can scope key ownership in Private if needed.
eli: for performance: recommend two-prong approach for contract: 1) enable burst autoscale (costed) for peak windows, 2) add per-route batching caps and a small pool pinned for short-gen to avoid cross-contamination. this should get p95 consistently under 120ms.
ops-bot: cost_estimate: burst 30m/day @ expected 30% overcommit = ~$0.12/min -> ~$54/mo. (rough)
noah: also suggest soft-SLA language: "p95 embed latency <= 120ms under committed capacity; during burst windows with autoscaling p95 typically <=120ms but subject to transient cache-warmup events."
maya: (typo) maya: i'll run a 30m validation tomorrow with burst enabled and pinned short-gen pool. same traffic mix customer will send.
eng-zoe: for the kernel toggle, result: multi-device reduce lowered nvlink by ~22% and reduced p99 spikes by ~40% on our trace.
maya: uploaded results CSV to shared: /drive/greenfield/poc/194321-results.csv
sales-amy: i'll bundle the performance summary + one-paragraph on security (KMS + SOC2 timeline) + ballpark burst cost for the prospect.
ops-bot: change_request: enable_burst_autoscale(greenfield-poc) submitted by maya at 1943210305  pending approval.
infra-luis: approved. enabling burst for next run window.
maya: final ask for this thread: can infra set a pinned-route for short-gen with 1 GPU headroom reserved so we avoid large batch takeovers? tagging @infra-luis.
infra-luis: will create route "short-gen-hot" pinned to 1 GPU equiv and reserve 1 GPU for headroom during run.
noah: great. once 30m run completes, can someone prepare a single-slide summary for sales deck: key numbers (p50/p95/p99), config tested, recommendations, cost delta?
sales-amy: on it. i'll draft slide and send for quick review.
maya: running the 30m now, will post final metrics in this thread when done.
eng-zoe: if we still see occasional >300ms spikes after all mitigations, recommend customer consider a per-request max_gen or chunked streaming to keep single-request tail bounded.
maya: noted. thanks everyone. :pray:
